messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr Chalmers,

I would be grateful for your assistance with cross-validation with mirt and mirtCAT.

My aim is to create an mcat simulation for an adaptive test that estimates 3 different traits with 3 different standardised scales. The goal would be to get score estimates for the 3 variables with less questions. I have been able to do this all with one dataset, but I am now at the stage of wanting to construct the model on some of the data, and test it on new data.

These are the steps I am now following:

Split up dataset into training data and testing data
Fit a Mirt model with the training data, called mirt_model_Train
Create mirtmod2values_Train <- mod2values(mirt_model_Train)
Set mirtmod2values_Train$est <- FALSE
Fit a new Mirt model with data = test_data, pars=mirtmod2values_Train… call this model mirt_model_TEST
Use fscores() with mirt_model_TEST and data = test_data, and use generate_pattern() with mirt_model_TEST and these fscores…call this pattern ‘patterns_empirical’
Run MCAT simulation called results_TEST with mirtcat(mo=mirtmodel_TEST, local_pattern = patterns_empirical….
Using mirt_model_TEST, Extract results with expected.test etc… compare True vs expected scores for the test_data
Re-do steps 6-8 except use the training data instead of test data.
Compare the 2 simulation results. The first being the simulation created with the training data and tested on the test data, and then the second being the simulation created with the training data and tested on the training data. Compare MAE and RMSE.

Could you please clarify if my approach is methodologically sound? I’m unsure if this is the best way to solve my research problem.

One issue I am noticing is In step 5, the mirt_model_Test instantly converges (within 0.001 tolerance after 0 MHRM iterations, and estimates 0 parameters).

I can happily provide you with code privately if that is easier for you to examine.

Many thanks in advance,
Will

messages.body_plain:
Hi -

I want to estimate a partial credit model with an estimated common slope instead of using the Rasch option which forces all slopes = 1. My data consists of three items with three response options (1, 2, and 3). I attempted to constrain the slopes to equality using the following commands.

First, obtain parameter names/numbers for the model

library(mirt)
values.gpcm <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", verbose=FALSE, pars='values')
print(values.gpcm)

That produced the following.

Next I specified that slopes 1 8 and 15 are constrained.

library(mirt)
results.pcm <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", verbose=FALSE, simplify=F, constrain=list(c(1, 8, 15)))
coef.pcmirt <- coef(results.pcm, IRTpars=TRUE, simplify=TRUE)
coef.pcmglfa <- coef(results.pcm, IRTpars=FALSE, simplify=TRUE)
print(results.pcm)
print(coef.pcmirt)
print(coef.pcmglfa)

The results match estimates from Stata except the model degrees of freedom are incorrect. Instead of 7 (6 thresholds and 1 slope), mirt reports 9 (6 thresholds and 3 slopes) despite the three slopes constrained to equality.

I tried setting the estimation of slopes 8 and 15 to false,

values.gpcm [1, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [1, "est"] = TRUE
values.gpcm [8, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [8, "est"] = FALSE
values.gpcm [15, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [15, "est"] = FALSE

and running this code instead

results.pcm1 <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", pars = values.gpcm,  verbose=FALSE, simplify=F, constrain=list(c(1, 8, 15)) )
coef.pcmirt1 <- coef(results.pcm1, IRTpars=TRUE, simplify=TRUE)
coef.pcmglfa1 <- coef(results.pcm1, IRTpars=FALSE, simplify=TRUE)
print(results.pcm1)
print(coef.pcmirt1)
print(coef.pcmglfa1)

and that worked to provide the correct model df, but I got this error message when trying to requet IRT parameters.

> coef.pcmirt1 <- coef(results.pcm1, IRTpars=TRUE, simplify=TRUE) Error in ret[obj@est, obj@est] <- vcov[pick, pick, drop = FALSE] : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

If I omit that line and omit print the IRT line, the code runs fine and produces the results expected. I can manually convert the slope-intercept to IRT, but I would like for mirt to produce those instead with the correct df.

Any ideas how to obtain PCM estimates, non-Rasch, with correct model df?

Thanks!
Bryan

messages.subject: Treatment of missing values in item-total correlations
messages.subject_clean: Treatment of missing values in item-total correlations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Chalmers,

Although itemstats() uses "pairwise.complete.obs" inside cor(), missing values are deleted listwise because rowSums() does not use na.rm = TRUE (lines 88, 94, and 99 in https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/blob/main/R/itemstats.R).

Consequently, a missing value for any of the items leads to a missing total score, and the calculation of the item-total correlation for a given item excludes not just the students who have a missing response for that item but also the students who have a missing response for any of the remaining items.

I wanted to mention in case this is not the intended behavior.

Best,
Eren

Hi Eren,

This was deliberate as I didn't want the summary statistics that pertain to the total score itself to be affected by missing response patterns (otherwise, for instance, the mean of the total score is a function of the missing data proportions and patterns). I do, however, see your point about the correlation values as these are metric independent. I've made the na.rm change to the total scores but only apply this to the correlations, and have made a note of this in the documentation. Thanks for the idea!

Phil

messages.subject: Re: DIF with two-dimensional 2PL or Unidimensional or ....
messages.subject_clean: DIF with two-dimensional 2PL or Unidimensional or ....
messages.body_plain:
Good question. If the model demonstrates  simple structure (isolated unidimensional patterns), and there's no real dependence between the simple structures (e.g., no constrained slopes or something like that) then it technically makes little difference asymptotically, though if the correlation between the traits is non-zero and reasonably strong then you could gain some additional power by utilizing the multidimensional structure. However, numerical integration becomes a limiting time/computational factor, so there's that to consider too.

Basically, if your sample size is large enough then I don't see any real harm though in treating the structure as effectively unidimensional packets. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Cross-validation
messages.subject_clean: Cross-validation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Will,

I think you lost me at the factor scores component as I don't see why this would be necessary. The benefit, of course, is that you can compute the usual metrics for cross validation based on observed predictions, but the scores themselves are subject to shrinkage/bias effects so they wouldn't be my go-to statistics except for reasonably long tests. It's possible to do cross validation without such approaches that focus on the likelihood information itself, though I haven't implemented this anywhere in the package. Happy to add this to the long TODO list though...

Phil
